extensions.description: The extensions the project switches on: each a module's name, or its name and the folder its package is in, relative to the project's main checkout. Without the key a project loads no extensions

siblings.description: The folders beside this checkout that its own code loads from, each with the environment variable the code finds it by, as in {"apple-engineering": "APPLE_ENGINEERING_ROOT"}. A run that pins this checkout, or a run of this project, pins each at one commit and sets the variable to its checkout of it (doc/guides/shared-host.md, Extension folders beside a project)

gitHooks.description: The folder of the project's tracked Git hooks, relative to the checkout's top, such as .githooks. qk doctor sets core.hooksPath to it where it is unset, as in a fresh clone, and warns where it names another folder

simulatorPool.description: The name every member of the project's simulator pool starts with, as in 'NAME iPhone 17 Pro 1'; required with the simulator-pool capability

unity.description: The Unity extension's key, which a project gets with queuekeeper_unity: where its Unity project is, and the window layout a new worktree's editor starts with

project.description: The folder that holds ProjectSettings, relative to the checkout, such as 'lab'; the checkout itself when left out

layout.description: A window layout (.dwlt), relative to the checkout, that qk unity open gives a worktree with none of its own before its first launch

oneOf.description: A lane: a command and how it runs
A lane group: other lanes run side by side under its one admission (doc/guides/parallel-tests.md)

parallel.description: A lane group's lanes, each a lane with a command, which run side by side under the group's one admission; the group needs the heaviest resource among them (doc/guides/parallel-tests.md)

jobs.description: How many of a lane group's lanes run at once, from 1 to their number; without it, all of them

resource.description: The admission the lane takes, first come, first served, another Mac first (the owner's decision, 2026-11-07): heavy, one slot, which light, the older name of a short check, and no resource mean too; exclusive, the host to itself; or self, for a lane whose script admits each of its parts itself, which qk run runs where it starts, unadmitted (doc/guides/shared-host.md, Heavy-work admission)

minimumTests.description: The fewest executed tests the lane's log must report for a whole run that exits 0 to pass; a skipped test counts toward none. With exactTests, the count the run must equal (doc/guides/lanes.md, Receipts and test counts)

exactTests.description: Whether a whole run of the lane must execute exactly its minimumTests, which the lane must then give: any other count fails, naming the count observed, so that adding, deleting or renaming a test the lane selects fails the lane instead of leaving minimumTests wrong. Left out or false, minimumTests is a floor. A run with arguments needs one test, or its --expect, as before

arguments.description: Whether the lane's command takes arguments. A lane that says false selects its own tests: qk run LANE -- ARGUMENTS, and --repeat, whose series reaches the command as arguments, are refused at once with exit status 2, before the lane is staged, admitted or sent to another Mac. Left out or true, the arguments are appended to the command

stall.description: Opt-in quiet monitoring for an admitted leaf lane. Report-only by default; stopping requires a healthy-run measurement and a reviewed bound (doc/guides/parallel-tests.md).

primaryControl.description: Explicitly declare that the supervised primary process only coordinates descendant work. Its CPU cannot mask quiet descendants; no descendants leaves the observation unavailable. Omit for serial or primary-process computation.

foreground.description: The lane takes a Mac's screen, keyboard, pointer, focus or speech, as Mac VoiceOver and Mac XCUITest lanes do. It needs a heavy or exclusive resource. qk run sends it to another Mac, which queuekeeper takes the foreground of for the run, waiting while another run holds it, and never to this Mac; qk run --here, or here, runs it on this Mac only for the session holding mac-foreground within the owner's window

apps.description: A foreground lane's app under test, each name as a crash-report alert names the process that quit, such as EPUBLib. A failed run during which queuekeeper cleared a crash-report alert for another process, one that stood longer than one look, is unmeasured; one for these, or for a process queuekeeper cannot name, stays failed (doc/guides/foreground.md, Crash-report alerts)

here.description: Why an admitted lane runs only on this Mac rather than on another Mac of the farm: a physical device, or a measurement tied to this Mac's hardware, such as goldens rendered on its GPU. Simulator, background Mac UI and foreground lanes go to another Mac like the rest. A lane group that runs such a lane stays here with it

model.description: A heavy lane that runs a model: on-device generation, another local generative model on the GPU, or Core ML whose compute units include the GPU. qk run admits it with one slot and the host's model lock, so model runs exclude each other while other heavy work runs beside them. A lane group that runs it needs model too, or an exclusive resource, and a group that runs two or more needs jobs 1. A model run that is timed or compared with a baseline is exclusive instead, which holds the model already

display.description: The Mac desktop extension's key, which a project gets with queuekeeper_mac_desktop or an extension that requires it, such as queuekeeper_apple. A heavy or exclusive lane whose tests wait for what the display's refresh times, such as a scroll view's animation: qk run runs its command, on any Mac and in a lane group too, under a one-second caffeinate -u, which wakes a sleeping display behind a lock too, and then caffeinate -d, which keeps it on for the command's life, and the lane's receipt shows them in its command. Neither unlocks the screen, so a test that reads its tree through the accessibility API still needs an unlocked one

unity.description: The Unity extension's key, which a project gets with queuekeeper_unity. A lane whose command runs the project's Unity editor: qk run runs its command under qk unity ready --, which checks on the Mac that runs it that an editor is installed, that no editor has the project open, that no stale lock is left and that no orphaned licensing helper remains, and ends the lane unmeasured, with nothing run, when one of them does not hold. An exclusive lane also ends unmeasured while an editor on that Mac is in Play mode

chips.description: The Mac hardware extension's key, which a project gets with queuekeeper_mac_hardware. The chips the lane's results are valid on, such as ["apple-m5-max"], for a lane whose output differs by GPU. qk run runs the lane only on a Mac with one of them, waits for that Mac when it is busy, and never runs it on another. A lane without the key runs on any Mac. qk host chip prints a Mac's

budgetMinutes.description: The gate lane's time budget in minutes, from its measured time. When the median wall time of its recent passing runs in the merge queue exceeds it, qk land and qk doctor warn and name its slowest parts (the toolkit's doc/guides/releasing.md, Keeping the split). Only the gate lane takes it

deviceRunMinutes.description: Minimum admission estimate in minutes for the full device lane, including the build, every device, and cleanup inside the lane. The reservation's own cleanup allowance is added separately

wholeHost.description: A heavy lane that is a Mac's work, such as a gate that runs the project's suites side by side: it takes every guaranteed slot of the Mac it runs on, so a second such lane never runs beside it there, and qk run sends it to the Mac that has them all free, while a lighter heavy lane still shares. A lane group that runs it needs wholeHost too, or an exclusive resource, which holds the host already (doc/guides/shared-host.md, Which Mac runs a lane)

idioms.description: Why the lane runs its whole selection on an iPhone and an iPad simulator: that every class it selects depends on the idiom, and where the project classifies them. Without it, qk doctor warns of a lane whose command names both with --device, outside release.lanes (doc/guides/lanes.md, One selection on two idioms)

devices.description: The device-record entries, such as iPhone, that a lane's script uses when its command is not qk device-pass, whose --device options say so: the lane waits for admission only until the last start that can finish within the window the session holds them for (doc/guides/devices.md, The device pass). It needs an admitted lane

unlockedScreen.description: A lane whose tests need an unlocked console screen, such as one that reads its own tree through the accessibility API; a lane group that runs such a lane says so too. queuekeeper places it only on a Mac whose screen reads unlocked, locked and unknown alike counting as no room for it, and otherwise it waits instead of running unmeasured. It needs an admitted lane (doc/guides/shared-host.md, Which Mac runs a lane)

compileFirst.description: An argv that compiles the lane's test target, such as xcodebuild build-for-testing on the derived data its command uses. It runs before the command in the lane's one admission and timeout, and a failure ends the run as build-failed with no test run. It needs an admitted lane, and a group runs its lanes' commands without it (doc/guides/lanes.md, Compile before the tests)

testLanes.description: What qk doctor's check that every test has a lane cannot work out for itself (doc/guides/lanes.md, Every test has a lane)

skip.description: Test paths kept as records, not counted as coverage, each mapped to the reason; a key ending in / is a directory

selects.description: For a lane whose command the check cannot read, the paths its tests are under; a key ending in / is a directory, and an empty list says the lane runs no test

citations.description: true has qk docs check also check citations of a document by path and section title, as in (doc/guides/shared-host.md, Heavy-work admission), or by path and anchor, in the project's Markdown and source files: each must name a document of this checkout and a heading or bold lead-in of it. Off unless set (doc/guides/maintenance.md, Docs check)

spelling.description: Exemptions from qk spelling, each mapped to the reason it is kept

skip.description: Tracked paths neither read nor judged by name; a key ending in / is a directory

exemptPhrases.description: Case-sensitive text removed before a line is read, such as a standard's term

exemptRuns.description: Whole identifiers another project named, such as MonoBehaviour

exemptTokens.description: Case-sensitive subwords, such as a proper name or a foreign word

queue.description: The merge queue (doc/guides/maintenance.md, The merge queue)

lanes.description: The lanes a batch passes before it lands, in order. Without it, the lane named gate

carryOver.description: Paths main may change under a passed result without gating again, a directory ending in /, each with why no queue lane reads it. Deprecated: read as queue.unread.paths, which replaces it

hookCoveredBy.description: The queue lanes that cover the pre-push hook, each with what of the hook it runs. With it, the queue pushes without running the hook

docsOnly.description: Conventional Markdown docs use spelling and docs checks by default. False disables this path; an object replaces default paths and lanes. Docs landings skip code hooks and are no full gate. Deprecated: read as queue.unread, which replaces it

paths.description: Each path, a directory ending in /, with why no code lane reads it

lanes.description: The lanes a docs-only batch runs instead, in order; never gate, whose receipt qk release reads

exclude.description: Paths consumed by code or tests, with why; these retain code gates even under listed documentation directories

unread.description: The paths no code lane reads. A batch that changes only these runs the docs lanes in place of the gate, and main changing one a passed batch does not touch leaves its result standing. The conventional Markdown defaults, the root README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CHANGELOG.md and Markdown under doc/ and docs/, count unless defaults is false. False gates every batch and carries nothing over. Replaces docsOnly and carryOver

paths.description: Each path, a directory ending in /, with why no code lane reads it; these add to the Markdown defaults, and are how a project names any other documentation folder, such as guides/

exclude.description: Paths among paths or the Markdown defaults that code or tests do read, with why; these always gate

lanes.description: The lanes a batch of unread paths runs instead, in order; never gate

defaults.description: False drops the conventional Markdown defaults, so that only paths counts

noVerdictRuns.description: How many runs in a row of a batch's gate may give no verdict (exit 3, 75 or 78) before the queue holds; 3 where it is unset. Read from main, never from a branch (doc/guides/maintenance.md, The merge queue)

followLandings.description: true has the queue fast-forward the project's main checkout to origin/main after each landing, when it is on main, clean and nothing runs from it: for a checkout other projects read, such as the folder an extension loads from. Read from main (doc/guides/maintenance.md, The merge queue)

spelling.description: Deprecated: give preflight instead, which it cannot stand beside. false stops the queue running the toolkit's spelling check, qk spelling, before the gate, on an ungated landing and before a docs-only batch's lanes in a project with no spelling lane and no preflight; a project's own spelling lane runs either way. Read from main (doc/merge_queue.md, Preflight lanes)

preflight.description: The project's preflight lanes, in order: cheap checks, each one command, that qk land runs on an entry replayed onto origin/main before it queues it, refusing it on a finding (exit 1), and that the queue runs first in every round, ungated landing and docs-only batch. [] for none. Until it is given, the queue runs the project's lane named spelling, or Queuekeeper's built-in spelling check, which a later release removes. Read from main (doc/merge_queue.md, Preflight lanes)

carryOverChecks.description: Commands that must pass on the rebased tree before a passed result carries over a move of main; any other outcome gates again, with no blame

command.description: An argv list, never shell source. {base} in a word is the commit the result passed on

paths.description: Run only when main moved one of these paths, a directory ending in /. Without it, on every carry-over

app.description: The app qk app keeps and runs: the last good build of each platform, kept on this Mac (doc/guides/app-builds.md)

project.description: The Xcode project, a path inside the checkout

workspace.description: The Xcode workspace, a path inside the checkout

directory.description: Where the project is and the build runs, inside the checkout. Without it, the checkout's top

configuration.description: The build configuration. Without it, Debug

prepare.description: A command run in directory before each build, such as generating the project

scheme.description: The scheme that builds the app

product.description: The built app's file name, such as Name.app; needed only when the build makes more than one app

settings.description: Build settings given on xcodebuild's command line, such as DEVELOPMENT_TEAM

afterLanding.description: Whether the merge queue keeps a build of it after each gated landing. Without it, true

scheme.description: The scheme that builds the app

product.description: The built app's file name, such as Name.app; needed only when the build makes more than one app

settings.description: Build settings given on xcodebuild's command line, such as DEVELOPMENT_TEAM

afterLanding.description: Whether the merge queue keeps a build of it after each gated landing. Without it, false

links.description: Checkouts beside the project that its build names by a relative path, such as ../NAME, each linked beside the kept source

release.description: The release gate (the toolkit's doc/guides/releasing.md, Two gates and Checkpoints)

lanes.description: The release checks, each a lane of its own, which run after gate on the release commit; qk release requires a pass of each at the commit, or the owner's waiver of its failure. Never gate, which qk release checks first, nor any lane a landing runs: spelling, provision, queue.lanes or gate, queue.docsOnly.lanes, or a member of a group among them

maxCommits.description: The commits main may hold since the last commit that passed every release lane before a checkpoint is due. Without it, 100
